old.title: Stop website notification popups
old.symptom: Desktop alerts claim the PC is infected, but the alerts identify a browser or website sender.
old.firstAction: Record the sender and close the alert without opening its link.
steps: In Microsoft Edge open Settings > Privacy, search, and services > Site permissions > All permissions > Notifications, or use the current notification settings route in the linked guide.
Remove or block the unwanted site’s permission; inspect related extensions and recent downloads if the alerts began with an installation.
Retest with the browser restarted. Use the malware route if executable detections, persistence or other compromise evidence remains.
old.expected: The unwanted site can no longer send notifications and normal browsing still works.
old.ifUnresolved: If the sender is not the browser, or alerts persist after permission removal, identify the actual installed application before removing anything.

new.title: Stop website notification popups
new.symptom: Desktop alerts claim the PC is infected, but the alerts identify a browser or website sender.
new.firstAction: Record the sender and close the alert without opening its link.
steps: In Microsoft Edge open Settings > Privacy, search, and services > Site permissions > All sites; choose the unwanted site and select See more.
Set that site’s Notifications permission to Block; inspect related extensions and recent downloads if the alerts began with an installation.
Retest with the browser restarted. Use the malware route if executable detections, persistence or other compromise evidence remains.
new.expected: The unwanted site can no longer send notifications and normal browsing still works.
new.ifUnresolved: If the sender is not the browser, or alerts persist after permission removal, identify the actual installed application before removing anything.

old.title: Undo an accidental allowed-threat decision
old.symptom: A known detection was allowed earlier and the same item remains present.
old.firstAction: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection and review the exact detection and its earlier disposition.
steps: Check Protection history and Allowed threats for the matching item; distinguish an allowed action from quarantine or a failed remediation.
For a confirmed accidental allowance, choose the supported Don’t allow action, update the active protection and rescan the affected scope.
Record the new disposition and whether the file or startup entry returns after restart.
old.expected: The unintended allowance is removed and the confirmed threat has a recorded remediation result.
old.ifUnresolved: If policy controls the setting or the detection recurs, involve the managed protection owner and investigate the entry point rather than adding exclusions.

new.title: Undo an accidental allowed-threat decision
new.symptom: A known detection was allowed earlier and the same item remains present.
new.firstAction: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection and review the exact detection and its earlier disposition.
steps: With the authorized administrator available, check Protection history and Allowed threats for the matching item; distinguish an allowed action from quarantine or a failed remediation.

Record the new disposition and whether the file or startup entry returns after restart.
new.expected: The unintended allowance is removed and the confirmed threat has a recorded remediation result.
new.ifUnresolved: If policy controls the setting or the detection recurs, involve the managed protection owner and investigate the entry point rather than adding exclusions.

old.title: Protect backups before testing a restore
old.symptom: Compromised machines can still reach the backup destination or its administration account.
old.firstAction: Have the incident lead separate backup access from the affected systems using a known-clean administration path.
steps: Identify offline, immutable or otherwise isolated recovery copies and record their dates without attaching them to an affected endpoint.
Check whether the backup account or repository was modified during the incident; preserve access logs and the incident timeline.
Restore a selected pre-incident sample into an isolated clean environment and test the actual data before planning production recovery.
old.expected: A usable recovery point is demonstrated and remains outside the attacker’s current access path.
old.ifUnresolved: If the backup system or administrative identity is also compromised, involve the incident and backup owners before changing retention or deleting snapshots.

old.title: Contain stolen account access as well as the PC
old.symptom: The incident involves privileged credentials, suspicious sessions or activity on more than one device.
old.firstAction: Use a known-clean device and have the identity administrator identify the affected account and scope.
steps: Preserve relevant sign-in and audit evidence before applying the organization’s account containment procedure.
Use the supported identity response to block or secure the account, reset credentials and revoke applicable sessions; review unauthorized authentication methods and app access.
Recheck access and sign-in activity from a clean session while endpoint containment continues.
old.expected: The account has an evidenced containment state and unauthorized access paths are addressed separately from endpoint rebuilding.
old.ifUnresolved: A password change alone is not a complete incident release. Escalate if administrators, federation or multiple identities are affected.

old.title: Evaluate a decryptor without risking the evidence
old.symptom: A supposed decryptor is offered for the observed ransomware family.
old.firstAction: Preserve the ransom note and encrypted originals, and check the family against the official No More Ransom resources.
steps: Use only the matched vendor/project instructions; a similar ransom-note name is not proof that a decryptor supports the exact variant.
Prepare separate copies of representative encrypted files and any required original/encrypted pairs.
Test the supported decryptor on those copies and open recovered files in their real applications before considering wider use.
old.expected: The test demonstrates usable files for the exact supported variant while original evidence remains intact.
old.ifUnresolved: If the variant is unsupported, files remain corrupt or a website asks for unapproved payment/credentials, stop and continue the incident-led restore plan.

old.title: Find the optional app delaying sign-in
old.symptom: The desktop appears quickly but the user must wait before starting normal work.
old.firstAction: Time the same sign-in-to-ready task before making changes.
steps: Open Task Manager > Startup apps and record enabled entries and their reported impact.
Disable one agreed optional item, keeping required security, accessibility and managed-support software in place, then repeat the same restart/sign-in test.
Keep only the evidenced change, and re-enable entries that did not improve the measured task.
old.expected: The user’s real ready-to-work time improves and required background functions still run.
old.ifUnresolved: If delays occur before sign-in or persist with the candidate disabled, investigate boot, domain, storage or profile dependencies.

old.title: Explain a laptop that slows down on battery
old.symptom: The same application is responsive on AC power but slow when unplugged.
old.firstAction: Repeat a short, identical workload on the approved charger and on battery.
steps: Inspect Settings > System > Power & battery for the active power mode and energy-saving state.
Check whether the charger is recognized and suitable for the model; record any low-power or charging warning.
Choose an approved power mode for the workload and retest without disabling thermal or battery protections.
old.expected: The performance difference is tied to an observed power state, charger issue or policy rather than an unexplained cleanup change.
old.ifUnresolved: If performance drops while hot or on a correctly rated charger, investigate cooling, battery condition or firmware using the exact OEM guidance.

old.title: Clear an update’s storage blocker safely
old.symptom: Windows Update asks for more space or fails during a low-space installation.
old.firstAction: Open Settings > System > Storage and record available space before deleting anything.
steps: Review the supported temporary-file and cleanup choices; keep Downloads, customer files and rollback material unless their removal is explicitly intended.
If the update offers external storage, follow that specific workflow using a trusted device and keep it attached for the required phase.
Retry the same update, restart when requested and confirm its entry in Update history.
old.expected: The identified update completes and the user’s data and rollback decision remain accounted for.
old.ifUnresolved: If space rapidly disappears again, identify the owning files or service; do not repeatedly erase logs needed to diagnose the failure.

old.title: Identify the Windows volume inside recovery
old.symptom: An offline repair cannot find Windows or appears to target the wrong drive.
old.firstAction: Treat drive letters in the recovery environment as unverified until the actual volumes are identified.
steps: Use the recovery disk/volume listing to compare sizes, labels and encryption state without formatting or modifying partitions.
Inspect the candidate volume for the expected Windows and user folders; unlock the intended encrypted volume through its approved recovery key if required.
Use that verified volume only in the product’s documented offline repair syntax and retain the target identity in the private ticket.
old.expected: The offline operation addresses the intended installation, not the USB, recovery partition or another attached disk.
old.ifUnresolved: Stop if the target cannot be distinguished or the source is failing; never assume that C: identifies the installed OS in recovery.

new.title: Identify the Windows volume inside recovery
new.symptom: An offline repair cannot find Windows or appears to target the wrong drive.
new.firstAction: Treat drive letters in the recovery environment as unverified until the actual volumes are identified.
steps: In the recovery Command Prompt, run diskpart, then list volume, then exit; compare volume sizes and labels without formatting or modifying partitions, and verify the candidate volume’s encryption state.
Inspect the candidate volume for the expected Windows and user folders; unlock the intended encrypted volume through its approved recovery key if required.
Use that verified volume only in the product’s documented offline repair syntax and retain the target identity in the private ticket.
new.expected: The offline operation addresses the intended installation, not the USB, recovery partition or another attached disk.
new.ifUnresolved: Stop if the target cannot be distinguished or the source is failing; never assume that C: identifies the installed OS in recovery.

old.title: Fix a PC stuck on a self-assigned address
old.symptom: A DHCP-configured adapter has a 169.254 address and cannot reach the normal gateway.
old.firstAction: Run ipconfig /all and identify the affected adapter, DHCP state and lease information.
steps: Check the actual cable/Wi-Fi association and compare one working device on the same intended network.
Inspect the DHCP Client service and its Admin/Operational event logs; distinguish one-PC failure from a VLAN, scope or server problem.
Restore the proven DHCP path, then renew only the affected adapter when a local or alternate access path is available.
old.expected: The adapter receives the intended lease, gateway and DNS settings and reaches the required service.
old.ifUnresolved: Do not invent a static address or release the adapter carrying the only remote session. Escalate shared lease failures to the network owner.

old.title: Move a required file through an approved route
old.symptom: Screen control works, but the required installer or diagnostic file cannot be transferred.
old.firstAction: Confirm the exact file, transfer direction and approved destination with the user.
steps: For an installer, open the verified publisher link on the target PC where possible instead of assuming clipboard copy is file transfer.
For private evidence, verify the chosen client’s file-transfer capability and permission or use the approved private transfer service.
Check the received file’s identity and readable content, then apply the agreed retention/removal decision.
old.expected: The intended file reaches the correct private destination without copying unrelated customer data.
old.ifUnresolved: If the selected session lacks the necessary capability, change to an approved route; do not deploy an unplanned unattended agent.

old.title: Avoid losing the session during a restart
old.symptom: The next repair requires rebooting, changing the network adapter or restarting security software.
old.firstAction: Agree how the user and technician will reconnect before making the change.
steps: For an attended code-based session, keep the user available to reopen the app and approve a new connection when needed.
For existing managed access, verify the assigned device, service startup and approved reconnect behavior before restarting.
After reconnecting, confirm the same machine and user context and retest the original repair outcome.
old.expected: The session resumes through the agreed route without creating unplanned permanent access.
old.ifUnresolved: If the only connection would be lost and no local person or recovery channel exists, defer the disruptive action.

old.title: Separate a bad document from a broken printer
old.symptom: A single PDF fails, but the printer’s internal page and other documents print.
old.firstAction: Keep the original file and test a simple one-page document on the same queue.
steps: Open the PDF in SumatraPDF and use Ctrl+P to try a single page with the same paper size and queue.
Compare page rendering and the exact print error; check whether only particular pages, fonts or embedded content trigger it.
Use the document/viewer’s supported correction or obtain a clean source copy, then print the required pages and confirm layout.
old.expected: The test identifies a document/viewer-specific failure without changing every user’s driver or spooler.
old.ifUnresolved: If all applications fail, return to the queue/device branch. Preserve confidential document contents when escalating to the author.

old.title: Isolate a memory fault after an upgrade
old.symptom: Crashes or memory-test errors began after changing RAM or firmware memory settings.
old.firstAction: Record the installed modules, slots and current firmware settings before opening the device.
steps: Check the exact motherboard/device memory requirements and restore an approved supported configuration before comparing results.
Boot Memtest86+ through a supported, approved firmware path and record which test/configuration produces errors.
Following the hardware service procedure, compare modules and slots individually to distinguish a module, slot or configuration problem.
old.expected: Errors are reproducible in a documented configuration or the corrected supported configuration completes the planned test.
old.ifUnresolved: A passing sample does not exclude every intermittent fault; stop if disassembly, firmware security or unsupported hardware exceeds the service scope.

old.title: Find a device failing through a USB hub
old.symptom: A scanner, printer or storage device disconnects through a dock but works intermittently elsewhere.
old.firstAction: Record the device, hub/dock, cable and physical port used for the failure.
steps: Compare the same device on a known-good direct port and cable without moving unrelated production devices.
Use USB Device Tree Viewer to identify the actual hub chain and negotiated connection, then check the dock/device’s power and firmware requirements.
Apply the evidenced cable, port, power or supported firmware correction and repeat a sustained real transfer or scan.
old.expected: The original workload remains connected on the documented path, with the failed component or topology isolated.
old.ifUnresolved: Do not use a failing storage device for repeated transfer stress; preserve its data first.

old.title: Remove access that was only for this repair
old.symptom: A temporary support program or unattended setting still starts after the case ends.
old.firstAction: Compare the current installation/access state with the agreed end state for this device.
steps: End all case-only sessions and remove the temporary unattended credential or enrollment through that product’s supported controls.
Uninstall a case-only client when appropriate; keep the organization’s approved persistent management agent intact.
Restart if required and verify that the temporary access is gone while approved support and the repaired task still work.
old.expected: Remaining access has an explicit owner and purpose; one-case access no longer functions.
old.ifUnresolved: If the temporary and managed deployments cannot be distinguished, involve the management owner before removing agents or services.

old.title: Use the supported optimization for the drive type
old.symptom: A maintenance request proposes repeatedly defragmenting or cleaning every drive.
old.firstAction: Check drive health and open Defragment and Optimize Drives to identify the media type and current status.
steps: Use Windows’ supported optimization for that media and review the scheduled state rather than applying an HDD-style routine to every device.
Investigate low free space or real I/O faults separately; optimization is not a repair for a failing drive.
Retest the user’s workload and retain the observed health/performance result.
old.expected: The appropriate maintenance completes without disguising an unresolved storage fault.
old.ifUnresolved: Stop write-heavy maintenance if the disk disconnects, reports I/O errors or contains the only unprotected data copy.

old.title: Resume a stalled cloud-sync workflow
old.symptom: New files remain on one PC and the OneDrive icon shows paused or an error state.
old.firstAction: Open the sync client’s activity/status view and identify the actual pause or error.
steps: Resume synchronization through the supported control when it is simply paused; for errors, resolve the named account, storage, filename or connectivity issue.
Wait for the relevant file’s completed state and verify the expected version through the intended cloud account or another authorized device.
Keep backup/retention checks separate because synchronization can propagate deletion or unwanted changes.
old.expected: The expected file version reaches the intended account and the client no longer reports an unresolved sync state.
old.ifUnresolved: Do not unlink, reset or delete the local folder before accounting for unsynced local-only files.
